fixer.title: agentHost: keep MCP servers starting until their tools load

introducer.title: MCP server integration for agent-host sessions

cases.mechanism: The host treated transport connection as full readiness even while MCP tool enumeration remained on the turn's blocking startup path. Because backgrounding is offered only for blocking Starting servers, a slow or hung `tools/list` became non-deferrable and could hold the first response indefinitely.
cases.symptom: First-turn response can remain blocked for the duration of a slow or hung MCP `tools/list` operation, with no Skip/background action after the server reports connected.
cases.fixedBehavior: A connected server remains `Starting` until `session.mcp_server_tools_loaded` or inventory `live.toolsLoaded` confirms tool discovery. Slow or nonresponsive `tools/list` work is now represented as blocking startup, so the existing Skip/background action can call `moveLoadingToBackground` and let the chat turn progress; normal servers become Ready when their tools arrive.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, `_translateSdkMcpStatus` mapped SDK `connected` directly to `McpServerStatus.Ready` (base line 9252, introduced by 74c45d448154f27b023e82a3b5e1be4043401118). The new runtime event contract explicitly distinguishes connection from completion of `tools/list`. The workbench only exposes `backgroundMcpServer` when a server is `Starting` with `blocking: true` (`agentHostCustomizationService.ts:299`), and after a 5s no-content grace renders the slow-start control (`agentHostSessionHandler.ts:3952-3977`); invoking it reaches `rpc.mcp.moveLoadingToBackground()` (`copilotAgentSession.ts:5963-5968`). Therefore the old Ready translation removed the only UI path that could release a turn still blocked on MCP tool discovery. The added branch at line 9303 retains connected-but-tools-pending servers as blocking Starting, while `_markMcpToolsLoaded` later promotes them to Ready.
